## Glossary

**ActionRule**  
One permission rule: action string, { rel, action }, { self }, { rule }, { any }, { all }, or null.

**assign**  
Action gating role grants and token creation: high roles (owner, admin) need own, others manage.

**check**  
The ReBAC evaluator: check(permix, rebacSchema, model, hydratedRecord, action), merging row rules additively.

**Dot-path delegation**  
{ rel: 'sourceSpace.organization', action } jumps to an ancestor and skips intermediate delegation; stricter than single-hop.

**Entitlements**  
JSON boolean grants on OrganizationUser or Token, merged over role actions as an allow override.

**getContextParams**  
Returns [model, record] for the current tenant context, for frontend permission checks.

**Hydration**  
Loading a record's parent chain (createHydrator) so check() can walk its relations.

**intersectEntitlements**  
Keeps only entitlement keys true in both the membership and the token.

**leave**  
Self action letting a user remove their own membership or token ({ self: 'userId' }).

**lesserRole**  
Returns the lowest of several roles; caps a token's role at its user's role.

**Organization**  
Top-level tenant; owns users, spaces, tokens and content, fully isolated from other organizations.

**OrganizationUser**  
A user's membership in one organization, with role and entitlements.

**ownerActions**  
Helper generating own/manage/operate/read fan-out across user, organization and space owner FKs.

**permissionRules**  
Optional JSON column of row-level ActionRules that only widen access (typically read only).

**permissions**  
Class: roles, actions, Permix, ReBAC walks, entitlements, row-level overrides and validatePermission.

**permix**  
Per-request permission checker created in prepareRequest; setup loads grants, check answers them, setSuperadmin bypasses.

**PlatformRole**  
System-wide role on User: user or superadmin (superadmin bypasses all permission checks).

**ReBAC**  
Relationship-based access: actions delegate along relations (space → organization) instead of being granted per row.

**rebacSchema**  
The per-model table of ActionRules the app enforces (packages/permissions/src/rebac/schema.ts).

**Role**  
Per-membership (and per-token) RBAC role: owner, admin, member, viewer, ordered by roleHierarchy.

**Space**  
Sub-tenant container inside one Organization; its own permission scope, delegating own to the organization.

**SpaceUser**  
A user's membership in one space; requires the matching OrganizationUser.

**Spoofing**  
Superadmin impersonation via the x-spoof-user-email header; the original admin is kept as spoofedBy.

**StandardAction**  
The shared action tiers read, operate, manage, own that resource action sets extend.

**superadmin**  
Class: the PlatformRole superadmin, admin routes, spoofing and the superadmin app.

**tenancy**  
Class: Organizations, Spaces and their OrganizationUser/SpaceUser memberships; User, Organization and Space contexts with data isolation.

**usePermission**  
UI hook turning a permission check into { show, disable, disabledText } for a record.

**validateOwnerPermission**  
Route middleware for owner-polymorphic resources: checks the action on the record's ownerModel owner.

**validatePermission**  
Route middleware: hydrate the loaded resource and run the ReBAC check for an action, 403 on failure.

**validateSuperadmin**  
Middleware rejecting with 403 unless the user's platformRole is superadmin.

## 1. What this Warden covers

Covers the template's tenancy model (Organization → Space, with OrganizationUser and SpaceUser memberships) and the authorization system on top of it: platform role, per-tenant RBAC roles, JSON entitlements, ReBAC delegation evaluated by Permix, row-level overrides, and the superadmin role with its admin routes and impersonation.

## 2. The domain

Tenancy has two levels. An Organization is the top-level, data-isolated tenant; a Space is a sub-container inside one organization. Membership is an OrganizationUser or a SpaceUser row carrying a Role (owner, admin, member, viewer) and optional entitlements, and a SpaceUser always requires the OrganizationUser first. Permissions come in three layers (PERMISSIONS.md Overview): PlatformRole on User (superadmin bypasses every check), Role per membership (RBAC, mapped to the StandardAction tiers read → operate → manage → own), and entitlements (JSON grants that override the role upward). Each request gets a fresh permix from prepareRequest; the auth middleware fills it through setupOrgPermissions / setupSpacePermissions / setupUserPermissions, and a token's role is capped with lesserRole and its entitlements intersected, so a token never exceeds its user.

Decisions are made by the ReBAC engine: rebacSchema declares per-model actions as ActionRules (same-resource inheritance, { rel, action } delegation including dot-paths, { self }, json-rules { rule }, any/all, null), and check() evaluates them on a hydrated record, merging a row's permissionRules additively (overrides only widen). Space own delegates to organization own, so org owners inherit space access without denormalized rows. On routes, choose validatePermission for a single-owner resource loaded by resourceContextMiddleware, validateOwnerPermission for owner-polymorphic resources, ownerActions() when writing schema entries for such models, and the assign action for role grants and token creation. On the frontend the same engine runs: permissions.setup(me) loads grants, and components gate with usePermission / checkPermission, nav items with access(), inquiry rows with useInquiryPermission. Use createPermissions/check for plain role grants and createRebacCheck plus createHydrator (the published @inixiative/permissions package that @template/permissions builds on) for relation or ABAC rules.

Superadmin is the platform role: validateSuperadmin gates admin routes (which also run soft-delete unscoped), isSuperadmin branches inline, and spoofMiddleware with x-spoof-user-email lets a superadmin act as another user. Not here: how a caller is authenticated (sessions, API tokens, the auth middleware chain, validateUser/validateActor) belongs to authentication-users; the inquiry lifecycle and handlers belong to inquiries-flows (only their send/resolve/read rules live here); lenses and buildWhereClause field whitelists belong to the filtering and data regions.

### Class `tenancy`: Organizations, spaces and memberships; Personal/Org/Space contexts

- **Organization** `packages/db/prisma/schema/organization.prisma`: sub-tenant scope: Space instead; a user's role in it: OrganizationUser
- **OrganizationUser** `packages/db/prisma/schema/organizationUser.prisma`: space-level membership: SpaceUser instead
- **Space** `packages/db/prisma/schema/space.prisma`: Sub-tenant scope under Organization; use Organization for top-level tenant ownership.
- **SpaceUser** `packages/db/prisma/schema/spaceUser.prisma`: Space-level access; org-wide access uses OrganizationUser, which every SpaceUser requires.
- **CreateOrganizationModal** `packages/ui/src/components/organizations/CreateOrganizationModal.tsx#CreateOrganizationModal`: Creating organizations; don't rebuild slug derivation, reuse useValidateUniqueness for other unique fields.
- **OrganizationProfilePage** `packages/ui/src/pages/OrganizationProfilePage.tsx#OrganizationProfilePage`: Organization context only; SpaceProfilePage or UserProfilePage for spaces and users.
- **OrganizationSpacesPage** `packages/ui/src/pages/OrganizationSpacesPage.tsx#OrganizationSpacesPage`: Spaces of one organization; OrganizationsPage lists organizations, OrganizationUsersPage lists members.
- **validateNotLastOwner** `apps/api/src/modules/organization/validations/validateNotLastOwner.ts#validateNotLastOwner`: block removing or demoting an organization's last owner
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a db.organizationUser.count({ where: { role: 'owner' } }) guard written inline before removing or demoting a member (catalog: apps/api/src/modules/organization/validations/validateNotLastOwner.ts)
- **apps/admin/app/routes/_authenticated/organizations** `apps/admin/app/routes/_authenticated/organizations`: Org-level tenancy screens go here; space-scoped screens: _authenticated/spaces; member/user screens: _authenticated/users.
- **apps/admin/app/routes/_authenticated/spaces** `apps/admin/app/routes/_authenticated/spaces`: Space-scoped tenancy screens go here; organization-level screens: _authenticated/organizations.
- **apps/admin/app/routes/_authenticated/users** `apps/admin/app/routes/_authenticated/users`: Member and invitation screens for users go here; organization invitations: _authenticated/organizations.
- **apps/api/src/modules/organization** `apps/api/src/modules/organization`: Org-scoped resources; space-scoped use space module, caller-owned use me module.
- **apps/api/src/modules/organizationUser** `apps/api/src/modules/organizationUser`: Org membership rows; space memberships use spaceUser; creating memberships goes through organizationCreateOrganizationUser.
- **apps/api/src/modules/space** `apps/api/src/modules/space`: Space-scoped resources; org-wide use organization module, caller-owned use me module.
- **apps/api/src/modules/spaceUser** `apps/api/src/modules/spaceUser`: Space membership rows; organization memberships use organizationUser instead.
- **apps/web/app/routes/_authenticated/organizations** `apps/web/app/routes/_authenticated/organizations`: Organization-level views go here; space-scoped pages belong in _authenticated/spaces, member lists in _authenticated/users.
- **apps/web/app/routes/_authenticated/spaces** `apps/web/app/routes/_authenticated/spaces`: Space-scoped views here; organization-level views in _authenticated/organizations.
- **apps/web/app/routes/_authenticated/users** `apps/web/app/routes/_authenticated/users`: Member and invitation lists here; organization invitations in _authenticated/organizations; own profile in settings.

### Class `permissions`: Roles, actions, Permix, ReBAC walks, entitlements, row-level overrides, validatePermission

- **Role** `packages/db/prisma/schema/user.prisma`: Tenant or token access level: Role; platform superadmin gate: PlatformRole instead.
- **actionRuleSchema** `@inixiative/permissions/actionRuleSchema#actionRuleSchema`: Validating whole ActionRule overrides; for the abac condition alone use json-rules validateRule, which this delegates to.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* persisting a tenant-authored permissionRules override unvalidated, or a hand-written zod union describing ActionRule (@inixiative/permissions/README.md § Writing a schema; § Also exported)
- **createHydrator** `@inixiative/permissions#createHydrator`: Run before createRebacCheck; it dedupes loads per hydration and breaks cycles, but cross-call caching belongs in load.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a recursive hand-written loader that walks FK columns to fetch parent records, with its own seen-set to avoid cycles, before calling check (@inixiative/permissions/README.md § Hydration (Prisma example))
- **createPermissions** `@inixiative/permissions#createPermissions`: Plain role/action checks: use this; relation-based or ABAC rules: createRebacCheck.
- **createRebacCheck** `@inixiative/permissions#createRebacCheck`: Relation or rule-based access: use this; plain role checks: createPermissions. Hydrate records with createHydrator first.
- **buildPermissionRulesSchema** `packages/permissions/src/rebac/permissionRulesSchema.ts#buildPermissionRulesSchema`: Use in route schemas accepting permissionRules instead of hand-writing action enums; derives keys from rebacSchema.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written zod enum or object of action keys for a permissionRules body field, a second source of truth beside rebacSchema (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Row-Level Overrides › Boundary validation)
- **check** `packages/permissions/src/rebac/check.ts#check`: Core evaluator; define grants in rebacSchema or role maps, then call check rather than hand-rolling permission logic.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* if/else chains in a controller that look up an OrganizationUser or SpaceUser and compare its role, instead of declaring the rule in rebacSchema and calling check (catalog: packages/permissions/src/rebac/check.ts ("call check rather than hand-rolling permission logic"))
- **checkPermission** `packages/ui/src/hooks/usePermission.ts#checkPermission`: Inside components prefer usePermission hook or permissions.check; use this in plain functions or loops.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* role comparisons inside a plain function or loop instead of checkPermission(permissions, model, record, action) (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Frontend Checks)
- **createPermissions** `packages/permissions/src/client.ts#createPermissions`: build a typed Permix permissions client for checks
- **getOrgPermissions** `packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts#getOrgPermissions`: Org-scoped grants; use getSpacePermissions for space memberships.
- **getSpacePermissions** `packages/permissions/src/roles/space.ts#getSpacePermissions`: space-scoped grants; org membership rows use getOrgPermissions, a user's own record uses getUserPermissions
- **getUserPermissions** `packages/permissions/src/roles/user.ts#getUserPermissions`: self-scoped grants applied first for non-superadmins; tenant scopes use getOrgPermissions or getSpacePermissions
- **greaterRole** `packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts#greaterRole`: return the highest of several roles, ignoring nulls
- **isSuperadmin** `packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts#isSuperadmin`: platform-wide bypass checks; tenant roles use rolesAtOrAbove or getSpacePermissions instead
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* inline user.platformRole === 'superadmin' comparisons (catalog: packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts and apps/api/src/lib/context/isSuperadmin.ts)
- **lesserRole** `packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts#lesserRole`: capping a role by another (e.g. inherited org role); for threshold lists use rolesAtOrAbove
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a token's role used directly, or roleHierarchy.indexOf comparisons by hand, when combining a membership role with a token role (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Roles › Role Hierarchy; Token Permission Restriction)
- **ownerActions** `packages/permissions/src/rebac/ownerActions.ts#ownerActions`: Use for models with nullable multi-owner FKs (Contact, WebhookSubscription) instead of writing per-action fan-out by hand.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* the same { any: [{ rel: 'user', action }, { rel: 'organization', action }, { rel: 'space', action }] } written out for every action of an owner-polymorphic model in rebacSchema (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Owner-Polymorphic Models)
- **polymorphicBindings** `packages/db/src/registries/polymorphicIs.ts#polymorphicBindings`: Pair with polymorphicIs conditions; it supplies the bind values they reference.
- **polymorphicIs** `packages/db/src/registries/polymorphicIs.ts#polymorphicIs`: Use instead of hand-writing per-kind key/discriminator arms; bind values with polymorphicBindings.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-written per-kind arms matching ownerModel plus the matching FK column in a rule condition (catalog: packages/db/src/registries/polymorphicIs.ts)
- **rebacSchema** `packages/permissions/src/rebac/schema.ts#rebacSchema`: Add model action rules here; role grants live in organizationRoles/getOrgPermissions, evaluation in check.
- **rolesAtOrAbove** `packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts#rolesAtOrAbove`: minimum-role filters and queries; comparing two specific roles: lesserRole instead
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a literal role list such as where: { role: { in: ['owner', 'admin'] } } for a minimum-role filter (catalog: packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts#rolesAtOrAbove)
- **setupOrgPermissions** `apps/api/src/lib/permissions/setupOrgPermissions.ts#setupOrgPermissions`: Org-scoped routes; space routes use setupSpacePermissions, user-scoped use setupUserPermissions.
- **setupSpacePermissions** `apps/api/src/lib/permissions/setupSpacePermissions.ts#setupSpacePermissions`: Space-scoped routes; org routes use setupOrgPermissions, user-scoped use setupUserPermissions.
- **setupUserPermissions** `apps/api/src/lib/permissions/setupUserPermissions.ts#setupUserPermissions`: User-scoped routes; org or space contexts use setupOrgPermissions or setupSpacePermissions.
- **StandardAction** `packages/permissions/src/client.ts#StandardAction`: Base for new resource action sets; extend like InquiryAction when custom verbs are needed.
- **usePermission** `packages/ui/src/hooks/usePermission.ts#usePermission`: Non-hook contexts or many records: checkPermission instead.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a component that compares user.role or membership.role === 'owner' to show or disable a control (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Frontend Checks)
- **validateOwnerPermission** `apps/api/src/middleware/validations/validateOwnerPermission.ts#validateOwnerPermission`: permission on the resource itself: validatePermission instead
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a switch on resource.ownerModel calling permix.check('user' | 'organization', …) per branch inside a controller (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Validation Middleware › validateOwnerPermission)
- **validateRole** `apps/api/src/lib/permissions/validateRole.ts#validateRole`: parse an unknown value into a Role enum or throw
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* role: token.role as Role (a type assertion) when setting up permissions, instead of validating and failing closed to viewer (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Permission Setup › Role Validation)
- **Action delegation chain** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Schema`: tier actions so read inherits operate, operate manage, manage own; own terminal or delegated
- **Bridges** `@inixiative/permissions README — Bridges (cross-source rel walks)`: Cross-source edges only; same-source FK walks use plain rel with the injected resolver.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* fetching a record from another source (another fieldMap) and comparing join keys by hand before or after check, instead of declaring a bridge on the schema (@inixiative/permissions/README.md § Bridges (cross-source rel walks))
- **Dot-path relation delegation** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Dot-path vs. Single-hop Delegation`: Stricter ancestor-only check; single-hop { rel: 'sourceSpace', action: 'own' } instead when intermediate delegation should apply.
- **Hydrate ownership closure before checking** `@inixiative/permissions/README.md#Hydration (Prisma example)`: Always for ReBAC checks; hand-attach extras only for self-references or polymorphic joins.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* ad-hoc include chains built per route to load parents before a ReBAC check, instead of createHydrator / the hydrate step (@inixiative/permissions README › Hydration)
- **Inquiry send/resolve per type** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Schema (inquiry)`: Adding a new inquiry type: add its send and resolve branches here.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* per-type role checks written in the create controller instead of a send branch in rebacSchema (docs/claude/INQUIRIES.md § Adding a New Handler step 11; Permissions (ReBAC))
- **Layered frontend permission checks** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Frontend Checks`: pick the entry point matching the layer being gated
- **Owner-polymorphic permissions via ownerActions** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Owner-Polymorphic Models`: Models with nullable FKs to multiple owners (Contact, WebhookSubscription); compose extra custom actions by spreading.
- **Permission-gated UI** `docs/claude/ZUSTAND.md#PermissionsSlice`: hide or disable controls via Button show/disabled props from permission checks
- **ReBAC permissions with Permix** `FEATURES.md > Unique Selling Points`: grant actions through relationship-based access checks evaluated by Permix
- **Row-level permission overrides** `packages/permissions/src/rebac/check.ts`: Opt-in sharing of individual records; if every row needs the same override, change the schema rule instead.
- **Self-leave action** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Schema`: let users remove their own membership or token via self check
- **Space permissions delegate to organization** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Permission Flow`: Space-scoped resources; org owners inherit space permissions automatically.
- **Superadmin short-circuit** `packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts`: grant superadmins everything instead of computing role actions
- **Three-layer permission model** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Overview`: layer platform role, per-org RBAC role and JSON entitlements ABAC for authorization
- **Typed resource union** `@inixiative/permissions README — The check engine`: Pass a resource union to createRebacCheck so schema and subjects typecheck without casts.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* `as` casts on resource strings or an untyped createRebacCheck where a typo in a resource key passes the compiler (@inixiative/permissions/README.md § The check engine)
- **ActionRule** `@inixiative/permissions ActionRule`: express a permission as delegation, relation walk, self match, abac predicate, or composition
- **Button show/disabledText** `packages/ui Button`: permission-gated actions instead of wrapping in conditionals
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* {canEdit && <Button>...</Button>} or ternaries wrapping buttons for permission gating instead of show / disabledText (docs/claude/FRONTEND/COMPONENTS.md § Standard Conditional Props)
- **checkContextPermission** `_authenticated.tsx → useAuthenticatedRouting`: page-level gating; components use checkPermission instead
- **Entitlements** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Entitlements`: Grant a specific power to one member or token; change organizationRoles when every holder of a role needs it.
- **getContextParams** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Frontend Checks`: return [model, record] for current organization, space or user context
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written switch on context.space / context.organization / user to build the model and record for permissions.check (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Frontend Checks › Nav access)
- **NavItem.access** `apps/*/app/config/nav/features/*.ts`: nav visibility; component actions use usePermission or checkPermission
- **permissionRules** `@inixiative/permissions README — Writing a schema`: Per-record widening only; it cannot revoke, so change the schema to restrict.
- **permissions.check** `packages/ui/src/store/slices/permissions.ts`: inside nav access callbacks; components prefer checkPermission
- **permissions.setup** `packages/ui/src/store/slices/permissions.ts`: load user, organization and space permissions from /me into the frontend ReBAC engine
- **permix.check** `@inixiative/permissions createPermissions`: Grant-only lookup; use the rebac check for relation/abac rules.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* resolving record.organizationId by hand and calling permix.check('organization', action, id) where a { rel: 'organization', action } rule and check would walk it (@inixiative/permissions/README.md § The permix wrapper; § The check engine)
- **permix.getJSON** `Permix`: export loaded permissions as resource-action boolean map
- **permix.setSuperadmin** `packages/ui/src/store/slices/permissions.ts`: make every frontend permission check pass for a superadmin
- **permix.setup** `@inixiative/permissions createPermissions`: load role-derived grants keyed by resource or resource:id
- **permix.setUserId** `@inixiative/permissions createPermissions`: set the actor id used by self rules
- **PermixLike** `@inixiative/permissions PermixLike`: define the grant-reading slice the check engine consumes
- **resourceContextMiddleware** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Via Validation Middleware`: load the route's resource, throwing 404 or 409 before authorization
- **setupOrgContext** `packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts`: Org scope; setupUserContext for self actions, setupSpaceContext for spaces.
- **setupSpaceContext** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#setupSpacePermissions`: Space scope; setupOrgContext for orgs.
- **setupUserContext** `packages/permissions/src/roles/user.ts`: Actions on the user themselves; setupOrgContext for org scope.
- **useAuthenticatedRouting** `_authenticated.tsx`: enforce page-level permission on authenticated routes with context fallback
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-parsing ?org= / ?space= search params in a page or layout and calling tenant setters from a useEffect (catalog entry useAuthenticatedRouting (don't hand-parse org/space search params); docs/claude/APPS.md § Context Switching)
- **useInquiryPermission** `packages/ui/src/hooks/usePermission.ts`: inquiry records; other models use usePermission
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* ad-hoc role checks gating inquiry Send/Approve buttons, ignoring which side of the inquiry the current context fills (docs/claude/INQUIRIES.md § Frontend › useInquiryPermission)
- **validateNotToken** `apps/api/src/middleware/validations/validateNotToken`: Add before permission middleware for token creation, self-deletion of tokens, org deletion and other destructive actions.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* if (c.get('token')) throw 403 written inside a handler for a session-only action (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Validation Middleware › validateNotToken)
- **validatePermission** `#/middleware/validations/validatePermission`: Route-level authorization; permix.check inline for custom controller logic; validateUser/validateActor for authentication.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a handler that loads the resource itself and calls permix.check / throws 403 by hand on a route where resourceContextMiddleware + validatePermission(action) would do it (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Validation Middleware)
- **Authenticate before authorizing** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Via Validation Middleware`: Org/Space tokens carry no user and fail both gates; see AUTH.md to choose.
- **Bridge far-field data** `@inixiative/permissions README — Bridges (cross-source rel walks)`: When a bridge hop ends in an abac or self rule rather than an rbac grant.
- **Entitlements allow-override** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#How Entitlements Are Applied`: Whenever role permissions and entitlements are merged; the role is not a hard ceiling (deny override is not used).
- **High-role assignment needs own** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Schema`: Role assignment on organization or space and inviteOrganizationUser inquiries.
- **Hydration stays in the app** `@inixiative/permissions README`: When wiring permissions into any app or extending the core.
- **Inquiry permissions send/resolve/read** `docs/claude/INQUIRIES.md > Lifecycle`: Inquiry edit, send and cancel need send; resolve needs resolve; get needs read; lists need manage on parent.
- **Resource existence is non-secret** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Resource Lookup Runs Before Authorization`: Only resources that must hide existence from non-members need custom middleware.
- **Role assignment requires assign action** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Role Assignment`: Whenever a role is granted to a membership, including token creation.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hard-coded ['owner', 'admin'].includes(targetRole) ? 'own' : 'manage' branch in each controller instead of checking the assign action (docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md § Role Assignment)
- **Row overrides limited to read** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#When to use it`: When adding permissionRules to a resource's route schemas.
- **Row permission rules are additive only** `packages/permissions/src/rebac/check.ts`: Any resource with a permissionRules column.
- **Row rules only widen** `@inixiative/permissions README — Writing a schema`: Whenever tenants author per-record permission overrides.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* writing null or a narrower rule into a record's permissionRules expecting it to revoke access the schema grants (@inixiative/permissions/README.md § Writing a schema ("can widen but never revoke"))
- **Secure defaults** `CLAUDE.md §7 Core Engineering Standards`: Enforce auth, permission and tenant boundary checks by default.
- **Sensitive actions are session-only** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#validateNotToken`: Destructive or credential-minting routes.
- **SpaceUser requires OrganizationUser** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Space Permissions`: Adding members to a space.
- **Token cannot exceed user's role** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Role Hierarchy`: whenever deriving token permissions
- **Token creation checks assign on parent** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Token Creation`: Every token creation endpoint, alongside validateNotToken.
- **Token self-deletion via leave** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Token Deletion`: Token deletion permissions; never let a token delete itself (validateNotToken).
- **Tokens restrict, never exceed, user role** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Token Permission Restriction`: Any permission setup for token-authenticated requests.
- **Validate roles at runtime, fail closed** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#Role Validation`: Every permission setup function reading roles from DB or tokens.
- *Also here, by name:* InquiryAction (`packages/permissions/src/client.ts`); OrganizationAction (`packages/permissions/src/client.ts`); POLYMORPHIC_BINDS (`packages/db/src/registries/polymorphicIs.ts`); Row (`@inixiative/permissions`); SpaceAction (`packages/permissions/src/client.ts`); UserAction (`packages/permissions/src/client.ts`); allTrue (`packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts`); intersectEntitlements (`packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts`); organizationRoles (`packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts`); roleHierarchy (`packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts`); roleToStandardAction (`packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts`); spaceRoles (`packages/permissions/src/roles/space.ts`); userRoles (`packages/permissions/src/roles/user.ts`)

### Class `superadmin`: Superadmin platform role, admin routes, superadmin app

- **PlatformRole** `packages/db/prisma/schema/user.prisma`: Platform-wide gate: PlatformRole; per-organization or space access: Role instead.
- **isSuperadmin** `apps/api/src/lib/context/isSuperadmin.ts#isSuperadmin`: Inline branching on superadmin; gating a whole route belongs to middleware validators.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* inline user.platformRole === 'superadmin' comparisons (catalog: packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts and apps/api/src/lib/context/isSuperadmin.ts)
- **spoofMiddleware** `apps/api/src/middleware/auth/spoofMiddleware.ts#spoofMiddleware`: let superadmins act as another user by swapping the context user
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a custom as-user query parameter or header that swaps the context user for support, outside the x-spoof-user-email path (docs/claude/AUTH.md § Spoof Middleware)
- **validateSuperadmin** `apps/api/src/middleware/validations/validateSuperadmin.ts#validateSuperadmin`: tenant-scoped access: validatePermission instead
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an admin handler that checks platformRole itself and throws 403, instead of mounting under the admin router with validateSuperadmin (catalog: apps/api/src/middleware/validations/validateSuperadmin.ts; docs/claude/AUTH.md § Validation Middleware)
- **apps/api/src/modules/admin** `apps/api/src/modules/admin`: expose superadmin endpoints for cache clearing, audit logs, cron jobs and job enqueue
- **apps/api/src/routes/admin** `apps/api/src/routes/admin`: Platform-wide superadmin endpoints; tenant-scoped routes belong in their feature modules.
- **apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/communications** `apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/communications`: show superadmin views of communications, inquiries and platform messages
- **apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/dashboard** `apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/dashboard`: show the superadmin landing dashboard
- **apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/settings** `apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/settings`: manage superadmin profile, tokens, integrations and webhooks settings
- **apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/users** `apps/superadmin/app/routes/_authenticated/users`: superadmin pages for browsing and managing platform users

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#multi-tenancy -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Multi-Tenancy (in "Template Features")

#### Multi-Tenancy

**Four-Context Architecture** - User, Organization, Space, and Public contexts with seamless switching, hierarchical permissions, and complete data isolation. Each context has its own navigation, routes, and permissions while sharing a unified state management system.

- ✅ **Organizations** - Top-level tenant containers with full CRUD, settings, custom auth providers, and organization-scoped tokens. Complete data isolation ensures one org cannot access another's data

- ✅ **Organization Memberships** - OrganizationUser join table with roles (owner, admin, member) and role management. Users can belong to multiple organizations
- 🟡 **Invitation System** - Email-based invitations to organizations (in progress)

- ✅ **Spaces** - Flexible sub-containers within organizations for projects, teams, or workspaces. Full CRUD operations with data isolation from other spaces in the same org

- ✅ **Space Memberships** - SpaceUser join table requiring org membership first. Space access is always a subset of org access - can't be in a space without being in its parent org

- ✅ **Hierarchical Tokens** - Tokens scoped to User (cross-org access), Organization (all spaces in org), or Space (single space only). Token scope determines accessible resources

- ✅ **Context Switching** - Frontend seamlessly switches between User, Organization, Space, and Public contexts. Each context has appropriate navigation, routes, and data access

- ✅ **URL State Sync** - Current context tracked in URL params (`?org=orgId`, `?space=spaceId`). Enables shareable links that preserve context and proper back/forward navigation

- ✅ **Context-Aware Navigation** - Navigation menus automatically show/hide items based on current context and user permissions. Organization menu only shows in org context, space menu only in space context

- ✅ **State Management** - Frontend store tracks current user, active organization, active space, and public state. All components access context through centralized store

[Learn more: FRONTEND.md](docs/claude/FRONTEND.md) | [APPS.md](docs/claude/APPS.md)

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#overview -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Overview (in "Permissions")

#### Overview

Three-layer permission system:

| Layer | Scope | Storage | Example |
|-------|-------|---------|---------|
| PlatformRole | System-wide | `User.platformRole` | superadmin bypasses all |
| Role | Per-org RBAC | `OrganizationUser.role` | owner, admin, member, viewer |
| Entitlements | Custom ABAC | JSON on OrganizationUser/Token | `{ "canExport": true }` |

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#roles -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Roles (in "Permissions")

#### Roles

##### PlatformRole

System-wide role on User model:

```prisma
enum PlatformRole {
  user        // Default - normal user
  superadmin  // Bypasses all permission checks
}
```

Superadmins:
- Skip all `permix.check()` calls (always return true)
- Can access admin routes — and only there see soft-deleted rows (the admin router runs inside `db.withDeleted`); on ordinary routes tombstones stay invisible to them too
- Can spoof other users

##### Role

Per-organization role on OrganizationUser:

```prisma
enum Role {
  owner   // Full control, can delete org, assign any role
  admin   // Can manage settings and users (except owners)
  member  // Can operate (create, edit own resources)
  viewer  // Read-only access
}
```

##### Role Hierarchy

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/roles/shared.ts
export const roleHierarchy = ['viewer', 'member', 'admin', 'owner'] as const;
```

Higher index = more permissions. Used for:
- `lesserRole(a, b)` - Returns the lower of two roles
- `greaterRole(a, b)` - Returns the higher of two roles
- Token permission restriction (token can't exceed user's role)

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#actions -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Actions (in "Permissions")

#### Actions

Actions define what operations are allowed:

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/client.ts
export const StandardAction = {
  read: 'read',       // View resources
  operate: 'operate', // Create, edit own resources
  manage: 'manage',   // Edit any resource, manage settings
  own: 'own',         // Full control, delete, transfer ownership
} as const;
```

##### Role → Action Mapping

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts
export const organizationRoles = {
  owner:  { organization: { read: true, operate: true, manage: true, own: true } },
  admin:  { organization: { read: true, operate: true, manage: true, own: false } },
  member: { organization: { read: true, operate: true, manage: false, own: false } },
  viewer: { organization: { read: true, operate: false, manage: false, own: false } },
};
```

##### roleToStandardAction

Maps role to the highest action it permits:

```typescript
const roleActionMap: Record<Role, OrganizationAction> = {
  owner: 'own',
  admin: 'manage',
  member: 'operate',
  viewer: 'read',
};

roleToStandardAction('admin');  // 'manage'
```

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#permix -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Permix (in "Permissions")

#### Permix

Permix is the permission checker. Each request gets a fresh instance via `prepareRequest`.

##### API

```typescript
type Permix = {
  check: (resource: ResourceType, action: Action, id?: string, data?: unknown) => boolean;
  setup: (perms: PermissionEntry | PermissionEntry[], options?: { replace?: boolean }) => Promise<void>;
  setSuperadmin: (value: boolean) => void;
  getJSON: () => Record<string, Record<string, boolean>> | null;
};
```

##### How It Works

```typescript
// 1. Created in prepareRequest (empty, no permissions)
c.set('permix', createPermissions());

// 2. Populated by auth middleware via setupOrgContext/setupUserContext
await permix.setup({
  resource: 'organization',
  id: 'org_abc123',
  actions: { read: true, operate: true, manage: false, own: false },
});

// 3. Checked by validation middleware or controllers
permix.check('organization', 'manage', 'org_abc123');  // false
```

##### Superadmin Bypass

```typescript
permix.setSuperadmin(true);
permix.check('organization', 'own', 'any_org');  // Always true
```

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#permission-setup -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Permission Setup (in "Permissions")

#### Permission Setup

Both organization and user contexts follow the same pattern: role → actions, with optional entitlements and token restrictions.

##### setupOrgContext

Called by auth middleware to set org permissions.

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts
export async function setupOrgContext(permix: Permix, params: {
  user?: { platformRole: string } | null;
  role: Role;
  orgId: OrganizationId;
  entitlements?: Entitlements;
}): Promise<void> {
  if (isSuperadmin(params.user)) {
    permix.setSuperadmin(true);
    return;
  }

  await permix.setup(getOrgPermissions(params.role, params.orgId, params.entitlements));
}
```

##### setupUserContext

Called by auth middleware to set user permissions. Mirrors org pattern exactly.

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/roles/user.ts
export async function setupUserContext(permix: Permix, params: {
  user: { id: string; platformRole: string };
  role?: Role;  // Defaults to 'owner'
  entitlements?: Entitlements;
}): Promise<void> {
  if (isSuperadmin(params.user)) {
    permix.setSuperadmin(true);
    return;
  }

  await permix.setup(getUserPermissions(params.user.id, params.role ?? 'owner', params.entitlements));
}
```

**Note**: User context uses the same `Role` enum - a user is effectively "owner" of themselves by default, but tokens can restrict this.

##### setupSpacePermissions

Called by auth middleware to set space permissions. Located in `apps/api/src/lib/permissions/setupSpacePermissions.ts`.

```typescript
export const setupSpacePermissions = async (c: Context<AppEnv>) => {
  const permix = c.get('permix');
  const token = c.get('token');
  const spaceUsers = c.get('spaceUsers');

  // Space token → single space, token permissions only
  if (token?.ownerModel === 'Space' && token.spaceId) {
    await setupSpaceContext(permix, { role, spaceId, entitlements });
    return;
  }

  // SpaceUser token → single space, lesser of spaceUser + token
  if (token?.ownerModel === 'SpaceUser' && token.spaceId) {
    const spaceUser = spaceUsers?.find((su) => su.spaceId === token.spaceId);
    if (spaceUser) {
      await setupSpaceContext(permix, {
        role: lesserRole(spaceUser.role, token.role),
        spaceId,
        entitlements: intersectEntitlements(spaceUser.entitlements, token.entitlements),
      });
    }
    return;
  }

  // Session or User token → all spaces the user belongs to
  for (const spaceUser of spaceUsers ?? []) {
    const role = token ? lesserRole(spaceUser.role, token.role) : spaceUser.role;
    await setupSpaceContext(permix, { role, spaceId: spaceUser.spaceId, entitlements });
  }
};
```

##### Token Permission Restriction

Tokens have their own `role` field that restricts permissions below the user's actual role. This applies to both org and user contexts.

```typescript
// Token schema (simplified)
{
  role: Role,    // 'owner' | 'admin' | 'member' | 'viewer'
  entitlements: Entitlements // Optional custom grants
}
```

**Organization context** - token restricts per-org role:

```typescript
// apps/api/src/lib/permissions/setupOrgPermissions.ts
for (const orgUser of orgUsers) {
  const role = token
    ? lesserRole(orgUser.role, token.role)  // Token can't exceed user's role
    : orgUser.role;
  const entitlements = token
    ? intersectEntitlements(orgUser.entitlements, token.entitlements)
    : orgUser.entitlements;

  await setupOrgContext(permix, { role, orgId, entitlements });
}
```

**User context** - token restricts what user can do to themselves:

```typescript
// apps/api/src/lib/permissions/setupUserPermissions.ts
const role = token?.role ?? 'owner';  // Default: full control
const entitlements = token
  ? intersectEntitlements(user.entitlements, token.entitlements)
  : user.entitlements;

await setupUserContext(permix, { user, role, entitlements });
```

A read-only token (`role: 'viewer'`) can't modify user profile even though the user owns it.

##### Role Validation

All permission setup functions validate role values before use to prevent permission bypass from corrupted database data.

**validateRole helper** (`apps/api/src/lib/permissions/validateRole.ts`):

```typescript
import { Role } from '@template/db/generated/client/enums';

export const validateRole = (value: unknown): Role => {
  if (typeof value === 'string' && Object.values(Role).includes(value as Role)) {
    return value as Role;
  }
  return Role.viewer; // Fail closed (most restrictive)
};
```

**Security principles:**
- **Fail closed**: Invalid roles default to `viewer` (most restrictive), not `owner`
- **Runtime validation**: Type assertions alone don't protect against corrupted DB values
- **Defense in depth**: Extra safety layer even though API validation should prevent invalid data

**Usage in permission setup:**
```typescript
// Before: Trust type assertion
role: token.role as Role

// After: Validate before using
role: validateRole(token.role)
```

This prevents scenarios where database corruption or bugs could result in invalid role values bypassing security checks.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#permission-checks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Permission Checks (in "Permissions")

#### Permission Checks

##### In Controllers

```typescript
const permix = c.get('permix');

if (!permix.check('organization', 'manage', orgId)) {
  throw new HTTPException(403, { message: 'Access denied' });
}
```

##### Via Validation Middleware

Authentication gates run first: `validateUser` (needs `c.get('user')`) or `validateActor` (needs `getActor(c).user`; Organization and Space tokens carry no user and fail both). Which to pick: [AUTH.md](./AUTH.md#choosing-between-validateuser-and-validateactor).

The template uses a unified `validatePermission` middleware that leverages ReBAC for permission checks:

```typescript
import { validatePermission } from '#/middleware/validations/validatePermission';

router.patch('/:id',
  resourceContextMiddleware(),
  validatePermission('manage'),  // Checks permission via ReBAC
  handler
);
```

###### Resource Lookup Runs Before Authorization

`resourceContextMiddleware` throws **404** (not found) or **409** (multiple matches)
*before* `validatePermission` runs. This is intentional. An unauthenticated or
unauthorized caller probing a URL cannot distinguish "this resource doesn't exist"
from "this resource exists but you can't see it" — both surface as 404.

The template treats resource existence as non-secret (IDs frequently appear in
share links, emails, audit logs, and references from peers). Privacy is enforced
on **field visibility and queries**, not on the discoverability of a resource ID.
If a future resource type genuinely needs to hide its existence from non-members,
write a custom middleware that returns 404 when the permission check fails.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#entitlements -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Entitlements (in "Permissions")

#### Entitlements

Custom permission grants beyond roles. Stored as JSON on OrganizationUser or Token.

```typescript
type Entitlements = Record<string, boolean> | null;

// Example
{
  "canExport": true,
  "canInvite": true,
  "maxProjects": false  // Can be used for feature flags too
}
```

##### How Entitlements Are Applied

Merged into role permissions during setup using **allow override** (entitlements can grant permissions the role doesn't have):

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/roles/organization.ts
export function getOrgPermissions(role, orgId, entitlements): PermissionEntry {
  const baseActions = organizationRoles[role].organization;
  return {
    resource: 'organization',
    id: orgId,
    actions: { ...baseActions, ...entitlements },  // Entitlements override role
  };
}
```

**Override behavior**: Allow override means a viewer with `{ manage: true }` entitlement CAN manage. Alternative would be deny override where role caps permissions.

| Strategy | Viewer + `{ manage: true }` | Use Case |
|----------|----------------------------|----------|
| Allow override (current) | Can manage | Grant specific powers to limited roles |
| Deny override | Cannot manage | Role is hard ceiling |

##### Intersecting Entitlements

When a token has entitlements, they're intersected with user's entitlements:

```typescript
// Only keys true in BOTH are kept
intersectEntitlements(
  { canExport: true, canInvite: true },
  { canExport: true, canInvite: false }
);
// Result: { canExport: true }
```

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#rebac -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § REBAC (in "Permissions")

#### REBAC

Relationship-Based Access Control allows permissions to delegate through relationships.

Located in `packages/permissions/src/rebac/`.

##### Schema

Defines how actions can delegate to other actions or related resources:

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/rebac/schema.ts
const highRoles = ['owner', 'admin'];

export const rebacSchema: RebacSchema = {
  user: {
    actions: {
      own: null,
      manage: 'own',
      operate: 'manage',
      read: 'operate',
    },
  },

  organization: {
    actions: {
      own: null,           // Terminal - no delegation
      manage: 'own',       // manage → check own on same resource
      operate: 'manage',   // operate → check manage
      read: 'operate',     // read → check operate
      // Role assignment: high roles need own, others need manage
      assign: {
        any: [
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'role', operator: 'in', value: highRoles } }, 'own'] },
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'role', operator: 'notIn', value: highRoles } }, 'manage'] },
        ],
      },
    },
  },

  space: {
    actions: {
      own: { rel: 'organization', action: 'own' },  // Delegate to org
      manage: 'own',
      operate: 'manage',
      read: 'operate',
      assign: { /* same as organization */ },
    },
  },

  organizationUser: {
    actions: {
      read: { any: [{ self: 'userId' }, { rel: 'organization', action: 'read' }] },
      leave: { self: 'userId' },  // Users can leave orgs themselves
      manage: { rel: 'organization', action: 'manage' },
      own: { rel: 'organization', action: 'own' },
    },
  },

  spaceUser: {
    actions: {
      read: { any: [{ self: 'userId' }, { rel: 'space', action: 'read' }] },
      leave: { self: 'userId' },  // Users can leave spaces themselves
      manage: { rel: 'space', action: 'manage' },
      own: { rel: 'space', action: 'own' },
    },
  },

  token: {
    actions: {
      leave: { self: 'userId' },  // Users can delete their own tokens
    },
  },

  authProvider: {
    actions: {
      own: { rel: 'organization', action: 'own' },  // Only org owners manage auth providers
    },
  },

  inquiry: {
    actions: {
      // Source or target can read their own inquiry
      read: {
        any: [
          { self: 'sourceUserId' },
          { rel: 'sourceOrganization', action: 'manage' },
          { rel: 'sourceSpace', action: 'manage' },
          { self: 'targetUserId' },
          { rel: 'targetOrganization', action: 'manage' },
          { rel: 'targetSpace', action: 'manage' },
        ],
      },

      // Send: who may create/initiate each inquiry type
      send: {
        any: [
          // Source user can act on their own inquiry (cancel, edit, re-send)
          // Add type strings here when user-sourced inquiry types exist
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: [] } }, { self: 'sourceUserId' }] },
          // inviteOrganizationUser: high roles require own
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: ['inviteOrganizationUser'] } }, { rule: { field: 'content.role', operator: 'in', value: highRoles } }, { rel: 'sourceOrganization', action: 'own' }] },
          // inviteOrganizationUser: normal roles require manage
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: ['inviteOrganizationUser'] } }, { rule: { field: 'content.role', operator: 'notIn', value: highRoles } }, { rel: 'sourceOrganization', action: 'manage' }] },
          // createSpace — org owner only
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: ['createSpace'] } }, { rel: 'sourceOrganization', action: 'own' }] },
          // updateSpace — space owner or org owner (sourceSpace.own delegates to org.own)
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: ['updateSpace'] } }, { rel: 'sourceSpace', action: 'own' }] },
          // transferSpace — org owner only (explicit 2-hop bypasses direct space.own)
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: ['transferSpace'] } }, { rel: 'sourceSpace.organization', action: 'own' }] },
        ],
      },

      // Resolve: target decides (approve/deny/requestChanges)
      resolve: {
        any: [
          { self: 'targetUserId' },
          // transferSpace — target org owner only
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'in', value: ['transferSpace'] } }, { rel: 'targetOrganization', action: 'own' }] },
          // all other types — target org manager
          { all: [{ rule: { field: 'type', operator: 'notIn', value: ['transferSpace'] } }, { rel: 'targetOrganization', action: 'manage' }] },
          { rel: 'targetSpace', action: 'manage' },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
};
```

##### ActionRule Types

| Rule | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| `string` | Inherit action from same resource | `manage: 'own'` → check `own` on same resource |
| `{ rel, action }` | Delegate to related resource (supports dot-path) | `{ rel: 'organization', action: 'own' }` |
| `{ self: field }` | Current user owns the record | `{ self: 'userId' }` → user.id === record.userId |
| `{ rule: Condition }` | JSON rule condition | `{ rule: { field: 'role', operator: 'in', value: ['owner'] } }` |
| `{ any: ActionRule[] }` | At least one must pass | `{ any: [{ self: 'userId' }, 'read'] }` |
| `{ all: ActionRule[] }` | All must pass | `{ all: [{ rule: ... }, 'own'] }` |
| `null` | Always false (terminal) | `own: null` |

##### How It Works

1. **Same-resource inheritance**: `manage: 'own'` means "to manage, check if user can own"
2. **Relation delegation**: `own: { rel: 'organization', action: 'own' }` means "to own a Space, check if user owns its Organization"
3. **Dot-path traversal**: `rel` supports dot-notation for multi-hop chains. `{ rel: 'sourceSpace.organization', action: 'own' }` traverses `inquiry.sourceSpace` then `.organization`, resolving the final model type at each step. Useful when you want to explicitly bypass intermediate delegation and assert on a specific ancestor.
4. **Chain resolution**: Rules can chain (read → operate → manage → own)
5. **Cycle detection**: Prevents infinite loops

##### Dot-path vs. Single-hop Delegation

These two rules look similar but behave differently:

```typescript
// Single-hop on space: checks space.own, which delegates to organization.own
// → space owner OR org owner passes (delegation chain runs)
{ rel: 'sourceSpace', action: 'own' }

// Dot-path to organization: jumps directly to the organization record, checks own there
// → only org owner passes (the space record is never checked, only traversed)
{ rel: 'sourceSpace.organization', action: 'own' }
```

Use dot-path when you want a stricter check that bypasses intermediate delegation. In the inquiry schema, `updateSpace` uses single-hop (space owner or org owner can update), while `transferSpace` uses dot-path (org owner only can transfer).

##### Example: Space Permission Check

```typescript
// To check space.read:
// 1. read → operate (same resource)
// 2. operate → manage (same resource)
// 3. manage → own (same resource)
// 4. own → { rel: 'organization', action: 'own' } (delegate to org)
// 5. Check organization.own
```

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#owner-polymorphic-models -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Owner-Polymorphic Models (in "Permissions")

#### Owner-Polymorphic Models

Models with nullable FKs to multiple owners (Contact, WebhookSubscription, etc.) use the `ownerActions()` helper instead of writing the same fan-out for every action:

```typescript
// packages/permissions/src/rebac/ownerActions.ts
import { ownerActions } from '@template/permissions/rebac/ownerActions';

// Default: fan out across user/organization/space
contact: { actions: ownerActions() },

// Pick a subset
emailTemplate: { actions: ownerActions(['organization', 'space']) },

// Compose with custom actions
contact: { actions: { ...ownerActions(), share: { ... } } },
```

For each of `own`/`manage`/`operate`/`read`, the helper expands to `{ any: [{ rel: 'user', action }, { rel: 'organization', action }, { rel: 'space', action }] }`. Only the populated FK resolves — `rel` returns false for the other relations because the record isn't loaded — so the `any` collapses to the actual owner's chain.

This is what makes the `read → operate → manage → own` chain on User/Org/Space reusable as-is for every owner-polymorphic resource.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#row-level-overrides -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Row-Level Overrides (in "Permissions")

#### Row-Level Overrides

Some resources need per-row sharing on top of the schema-default permissions — e.g. a user wants to make one specific contact readable by anyone, without changing the rule for all their contacts. The pattern is a `permissionRules: Json?` column on the resource that `check()` merges additively with the schema rule.

##### Schema

```prisma
model Contact {
  // ...
  permissionRules Json?  // Record<Action, ActionRule> | null
}
```

##### How `check()` merges

Inside `packages/permissions/src/rebac/check.ts`, when resolving an action by name:

```typescript
const schemaRule = schema[model]?.actions[actionOrRule] ?? null;
const rowRule    = record.permissionRules?.[actionOrRule];
const merged: ActionRule = rowRule !== undefined
  ? { any: [schemaRule, rowRule] }   // OR — additive only
  : schemaRule;
return check(permix, schema, model, record, merged, visited);
```

**Additive only.** Row rules can grant additional paths but never restrict — the schema rule is the floor. A row rule like `read: { all: [] }` (vacuously true) opens the row to any authenticated requester; setting `read: null` doesn't take read away from the owner.

##### Boundary validation

Rows arrive over the API, so route schemas validate the shape before it lands in the DB. Use `buildPermissionRulesSchema(model, pick?)` from `@template/permissions/rebac/permissionRulesSchema` — it derives the valid action keys from `rebacSchema[model].actions` so there's no second source of truth:

```typescript
// apps/api/src/modules/contact/schemas/contactSchemas.ts
import { buildPermissionRulesSchema } from '@template/permissions/rebac/permissionRulesSchema';

export const contactCreateBodySchema = ContactScalarInputSchema.omit({ ... }).extend({
  // Only `read` is row-overridable — granting manage/delete via row rules
  // would effectively transfer ownership, so those stay owner-gated.
  permissionRules: buildPermissionRulesSchema('contact', ['read']),
});
```

The schema validates the recursive `ActionRule` envelope (delegations, `{ rel, action }`, `{ self }`, `{ rule }`, `{ any }`, `{ all }`) but passes the inner json-rules `Condition` through as `unknown` — runtime `check()` validates it when the rule fires.

##### When to use it

Row-level overrides solve a specific need: opt-in sharing of individual records without changing the schema rule for everyone. Use it when:

- The resource has natural per-row access decisions (sharing a contact, publishing an asset).
- The set of overridable actions is narrow — typically `read` only. Exposing `manage`/`delete` row rules effectively lets owners delegate ownership, which usually shouldn't be a row decision.

Don't use it as a substitute for proper rebac modeling. If every row needs the same override, that belongs in the schema rule.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#space-permissions -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Space Permissions (in "Permissions")

#### Space Permissions

Spaces are containers within organizations. Space permissions delegate to the parent organization via REBAC.

##### Space Roles

Spaces use the same `Role` enum as organizations:

```prisma
enum Role {
  owner   // Full control
  admin   // Manage settings and members
  member  // Operate within resource
  viewer  // Read-only access
}
```

##### SpaceUser Model

```prisma
model SpaceUser {
  role            Role
  organizationId  String
  spaceId         String
  userId          String

  // Must be OrganizationUser first
  @@unique([organizationId, spaceId, userId])
}
```

##### Permission Flow

```
Space Permission Request
    ↓
Check SpaceUser.role for direct permission
    ↓
If not found, delegate via REBAC to Organization
    ↓
Organization permission grants Space permission
```

##### Key Points

1. **Prerequisite**: User must be OrganizationUser before SpaceUser
2. **Delegation**: Space `own` delegates to Organization `own`
3. **Inheritance**: Org owners automatically have Space permissions
4. **Tokens**: Can be scoped to Space via `spaceId` field

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#validation-middleware -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Validation Middleware (in "Permissions")

#### Validation Middleware

Located in `apps/api/src/middleware/validations/`.

##### validatePermission

Unified permission middleware using ReBAC. Hydrates the resource with relations needed for permission traversal, then checks via ReBAC schema (handles superadmin, direct perms, delegation):

```typescript
import { validatePermission } from '#/middleware/validations/validatePermission';

// Check 'read' on loaded resource
router.get('/:id', validatePermission('read'), handler);

// Check 'manage' on loaded resource
router.patch('/:id', validatePermission('manage'), handler);
```

How it works:
1. Gets the loaded `resource` and `resourceType` from context
2. Hydrates the resource with relations for ReBAC traversal (org -> space, etc.)
3. Checks permission via `check(permix, rebacSchema, resourceType, hydrated, action)`
4. Throws 403 if check fails

##### validateOwnerPermission

For polymorphic resources owned by either User or Organization. Checks the `ownerModel` field to determine which permission to validate.

```typescript
// apps/api/src/middleware/validations/validateOwnerPermission.ts
export const validateOwnerPermission = makeMiddleware<Options>((options) => async (c, next) => {
  const resource = c.get('resource');
  const permix = c.get('permix');
  const ownerModel = resource?.ownerModel;  // 'User' | 'Organization' | 'OrganizationUser'

  if (ownerModel === 'User' || ownerModel === 'OrganizationUser') {
    const userId = resource?.userId;
    if (userId && permix.check('user', action, userId)) return next();
  }

  if (ownerModel === 'Organization') {
    const orgId = resource?.organizationId;
    if (orgId && permix.check('organization', action, orgId)) return next();
  }

  throw new HTTPException(403, { message: 'Access denied' });
});
```

Usage (Token/WebhookSubscription can be owned by user or org):

```typescript
// tokenDelete.ts - user deleting their own token
middleware: [validateOwnerPermission({ action: 'manage' })]

// webhookSubscriptionRead.ts - anyone with read access
middleware: [validateOwnerPermission({ action: 'read' })]
```

##### validateNotToken

Blocks token-based auth for sensitive operations. Session-only.

```typescript
// Tokens cannot: create other tokens, delete orgs, delete themselves
export const validateNotToken = async (c, next) => {
  if (!c.get('user')) throw new HTTPException(401, { message: 'Authentication required' });
  if (c.get('token')) throw new HTTPException(403, { message: 'Tokens cannot perform this action' });
  await next();
};
```

Usage:

```typescript
// tokenDelete.ts - prevent token from deleting itself
middleware: [validateNotToken, validateOwnerPermission({ action: 'manage' })]

// meCreateToken.ts - only sessions can create tokens
middleware: [validateNotToken]

// organizationDelete.ts - destructive action requires session
middleware: [validateNotToken, validatePermission('own')]
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#role-assignment -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Role Assignment (in "Permissions")

#### Role Assignment

Role assignment uses the `assign` action defined in the ReBAC schema. The schema checks:
- Assigning owner/admin (high roles) requires `own` permission
- Assigning member/viewer requires `manage` permission

```typescript
// ReBAC handles this automatically via the assign action
check(permix, rebacSchema, 'organization', { id: orgId, role: targetRole }, 'assign');

// Or inline in controller:
const action = ['owner', 'admin'].includes(targetRole) ? 'own' : 'manage';
if (!permix.check('organization', action, orgId)) {
  throw new HTTPException(403, { message: `Cannot assign ${targetRole} role` });
}
```

##### Role Assignment Rules

| Assigner Role | Can Assign |
|---------------|------------|
| owner | owner, admin, member, viewer |
| admin | member, viewer |
| member | - |
| viewer | - |

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#token-permissions -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Token Permissions (in "Permissions")

#### Token Permissions

Tokens use the `leave` action for self-deletion and the `assign` action (via parent) for creation.

##### Token Creation

Token creation checks if the user can assign the token's role:
- Creating an owner-role token requires `own` permission
- Creating a member-role token requires `manage` permission

```typescript
// Check via parent resource (orgUser, spaceUser, etc.)
check(permix, rebacSchema, 'organization', { id: orgId, role: tokenRole }, 'assign');
```

##### Token Deletion

The ReBAC schema allows users to delete their own tokens via `leave`:

```typescript
token: {
  actions: {
    leave: { self: 'userId' },  // User can delete if token.userId === user.id
  },
},
```

Additionally, org/space admins can delete tokens within their scope via delegation:
- Org admins can delete OrgUser tokens (via `manage` on organization)
- Space admins can delete SpaceUser tokens (via `manage` on space)

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md#frontend-checks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md` § Frontend Checks (in "Permissions")

#### Frontend Checks

The frontend runs the same ReBAC engine. `permissions.setup(me)` (`packages/ui/src/store/slices/permissions.ts`) loads the user's own, organization and space permissions from `/me`, mirroring the backend setup. A superadmin gets `permix.setSuperadmin(true)` and every check passes.

| Layer | Entry point |
|-------|-------------|
| Route | `validateUser` / `validateActor`, then `validatePermission` ([Validation Middleware](#validation-middleware)) |
| Page | `_authenticated.tsx` → `useAuthenticatedRouting` → `checkContextPermission`: the nav item's `access` decides "can view"; on failure it falls back to the org (from a space), then user, then public context, else renders `Unauthorized` |
| Nav item | `access(permissions, context, page?)` on `NavItem`; the Sidebar hides items that fail it |
| Component | `checkPermission(permissions, model, record, action)` / `permissions.check(model, record, action)` |

**Check:**

```typescript
import { checkPermission } from '@template/ui/hooks/usePermission';

const permissions = useAppStore((state) => state.permissions);
const canDelete = checkPermission(permissions, 'organization', org, 'own');  // false when record is missing
```

**Visibility.** `Button` takes `show?: boolean | (() => boolean)` and `disabledText` (setting it disables the button and replaces its text):

```typescript
<Button show={checkPermission(permissions, 'organization', org, 'own')}>Delete</Button>
```

**Nav access** (`apps/*/app/config/nav/features/*.ts`):

```typescript
export const settingsItem: NavItem = {
  label: 'Settings',
  path: '/settings',
  access: (permissions, context) => permissions.check(...getContextParams(context), 'read'),
  items: [
    {
      label: 'Auth Providers',
      path: '/authProviders',
      access: (permissions, context) =>
        !!context.organization && permissions.check(...getContextParams(context), 'own'),
    },
  ],
};
```

`getContextParams(context)` returns `[model, record]` for the current tenant context (organization, space, or the user).

**usePermission** (`packages/ui/src/hooks/usePermission.ts`) wraps the check into `{ show, disable, disabledText? }`:

```typescript
const deleteAction = usePermission({ permissions, model: 'organization', record: org, action: 'own' });
// params: disabledText? (default "You do not have permission to perform this action"), requireRecord? (default true)
```

**useInquiryPermission(inquiry, action, side)** fills the current context into the inquiry's source or target side, then checks `inquiry`.

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#authorization-permissions -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Authorization & Permissions (in "Template Features")

#### Authorization & Permissions

**Full RBAC/ABAC/ReBAC Authorization** - Comprehensive permission system supporting Role-Based (RBAC), Attribute-Based (ABAC), and Relationship-Based (ReBAC) access control powered by Permix with JSON-Rules support. This unified system lets you define permissions using simple roles, complex attribute-based rules, or relationship graphs - all within the same framework. JSON-Rules integration enables dynamic permission logic without code deployment.

- ✅ **Multi-Level RBAC** - Roles at platform (superadmin, user), organization (owner, admin, member), and space (owner, admin, member) levels with clear hierarchies

- ✅ **Attribute-Based Control (ABAC)** - JSON-based entitlements at org and space level allow custom permission logic based on user attributes, resource properties, or contextual conditions

- ✅ **Relationship-Based Control (ReBAC)** - Google Zanzibar-style relationship graphs (User → OrgUser → Org → Space) for modeling complex permission scenarios like delegated access or inherited permissions

- ✅ **JSON-Rules Integration** - Define permission logic declaratively using @inixiative/json-rules without code deployment. Evaluate complex conditions, combine multiple rules, and update permission logic dynamically

- ✅ **Hierarchical Inheritance** - Space permissions automatically inherit from parent organization. Org owners automatically get owner access to all spaces

- ✅ **Permission Middleware** - validatePermission() and validateOwnerPermission() enforce checks before controller execution. Routes declare required permissions in OpenAPI definitions

- ✅ **Superadmin Bypass** - Platform superadmins bypass all permission checks for support scenarios while maintaining audit trails

- ✅ **Context Scoping** - Permission checks automatically scoped to current organization and space contexts. Prevents cross-tenant permission leaks

- ✅ **Per-Request Isolation** - Fresh Permix client instance per request ensures complete isolation between concurrent requests

- ✅ **Redis Performance Caching** - Permission evaluation results cached in Redis (10min TTL) for sub-millisecond response times

- 🟣 Visual permissions builder UX (ticket FEAT-008, depends on INFRA-002)

[Learn more: PERMISSIONS.md](docs/claude/PERMISSIONS.md)

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/AUTH.md#spoof-middleware -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/AUTH.md` § Spoof Middleware (in "Authentication")

#### Spoof Middleware

Located in `apps/api/src/middleware/auth/spoofMiddleware.ts`. Allows superadmins to act as other users.

```typescript
export const spoofMiddleware = async (c: Context<AppEnv>, next: Next) => {
  const user = c.get('user');
  if (!user || !isSuperadmin(c)) return next();

  const rawEmail = c.req.header('x-spoof-user-email');
  if (!rawEmail) return next();

  const spoofEmail = normalizeEmail(rawEmail);
  const spoofedBasic = await findUserByEmail(db, spoofEmail);
  if (!spoofedBasic) return next();
  const spoofedUser = await findUserWithRelations(db, spoofedBasic.id);
  if (!spoofedUser) return next();

  await setUserContext(c, spoofedUser);
  c.set('spoofedBy', user);
  c.header('x-spoofing-user-email', user.email);
  c.header('x-spoofed-user-email', spoofEmail);

  await next();
};
```

##### Usage

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <session-token>" \
     -H "x-spoof-user-email: target@example.com" \
     https://api.example.com/api/v1/me
```

##### Requirements

- Caller must be authenticated as superadmin
- Target user must exist
- Original admin tracked in `spoofedBy` for audit

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#admin-operations -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Admin Operations (in "Template Features")

#### Admin Operations

- ✅ **Cache Clearing** - `POST /admin/cache/clear` flushes Redis caches (permissions, tokens, sessions) without server restart. Essential for invalidating stale permission caches after role changes
- ✅ **Cron Job CRUD** - Full create/read/update/delete for scheduled jobs. Persist schedule, description, and enabled state. Admin can view all registered crons, their last/next run times, and current status
- ✅ **Manual Cron Triggering** - `POST /admin/cron/:name/trigger` runs any cron immediately regardless of schedule. Critical for one-off executions (key rotation, cache warming) without waiting for next scheduled run
- ✅ **Job Enqueueing** - `POST /admin/jobs/enqueue` manually enqueues any registered job with custom payload. Useful for reprocessing failed records or triggering background work on demand
- ✅ **Inquiry Oversight** - Admin routes to read and manage all inquiries across organizations. View status, override state transitions, inspect resolution metadata for support scenarios
- ✅ **Webhook Oversight** - Read all webhook subscriptions across organizations. Inspect delivery history via WebhookEvent records (status, response code, error body). Retrigger failed deliveries for integration debugging
- ✅ **BullBoard Dashboard** - Visual job monitoring at `/admin/queues`. Filterable by queue and status. Inspect job payloads, retry failed jobs, view execution times and error stack traces
- ✅ **Auth Provider Management** - Platform-level auth provider CRUD (Google, Microsoft, GitHub OAuth configs). Providers marked `platformDefault: true` are available to all organizations
- ✅ **Organization Management** - Read all organizations across platform with user counts, settings, and status. Superadmin routes bypass organization permission checks
